text: All necropsies (autopsies) should be done under supervision of a government veterinary officer. A necropsy examines a dead bird's organs to help diagnose disease and needs only a sharp cutting tool; the carcass must be burned or buried afterward, never discarded, to avoid spreading disease. Wear disposable plastic gloves during the procedure, or wash hands thoroughly with soap afterward, since a few poultry diseases can infect people. If Avian Influenza is suspected (e.g. sudden high mortality), do not perform a necropsy — send the carcasses to NaVRI instead. A proper, methodical inspection of every organ is needed; a quick, superficial look is not enough to reach a diagnosis.
